note: PROC-12s hv-regenerate MERGE DRIVER IS INVERTED: IT FIRES, EXITS 0, AND WRITES A CONFIDENTLY WRONG FILE WHOSE CONTENT DEPENDS ON WHICH SIDE YOU CHECKED OUT. This supersedes any reading that the six Tier B paths in .gitattributes are protected. They are not; they are worse off than an undriven path. MECHANISM: scripts/merge-regenerate.sh regenerates by running the generator over the WORKING TREE, but during a merge the working tree is not the merge product -- git ort has not yet written the incoming files. docs/audits/ sorts long before windows/sentiment/, so when the type-audit tool ran, windows/sentiment did not exist on disk and the tool honestly reported a tree with no sentiment crate. It was not wrong about what it measured; it measured the wrong tree. PROOF IT RUNS, not that it is skipped: GIT_TRACE=1 git merge origin/main shows run_command scripts/merge-regenerate.sh with four merge_file temporaries and the type-audit path, taking 12.0 s, and the merge then succeeds clean with post-merge running. POSITIVE CONTROL, same two commits merged BOTH DIRECTIONS: main left-arrow the-deed gives identifier-text 738, language 196, vessel 313, sentiment row PRESENT; the-deed left-arrow main gives identifier-text 739, language 201, vessel 314, sentiment row ABSENT. The output is a function of which side is checked out, not of the merge. That reproduced, on demand, the two opposite clean resolutions the lefford queue and I had independently observed and reported as separate incidents. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN NO DRIVER: an undriven three-way merge of an aggregate table at least sometimes conflicts on adjacent lines and forces a human to look. The driver guarantees a clean plausible direction-dependent answer while wearing the name of the safeguard, which is why three separate regenerations were needed before anyone noticed. All six Tier B entries have identical exposure; five are book reference pages generated by cargo run -p hornvale. RECOMMENDATION, not yet done, needs a decision because PROC-12 is ratified: the driver cannot do its job, because the information it needs does not exist when it is called. Either delete the Tier B entries and let those paths conflict normally, keeping the post-merge hooks advisory as the real mechanism -- it is what actually caught all three instances -- or keep the driver but have it FAIL LOUDLY so the path lands unmerged and a human regenerates. Deleting is simpler and loses nothing that currently works.
